strengths: Principled causal formulation: The Standard Anti-Causal Model (SAM) effectively unifies confounder, collider, and mediator bias mechanisms under an anti-causal prediction framing, providing a rigorous path-specific counterfactual decomposition that justifies the conditional independence criterion $\hat{Y} \perp B \mid Y$.

Non-trivial computational contribution (sDISCO): Naive calculation of the conditional distance correlation V-statistic requires $O(n^3)$ memory to maintain local double-centered matrices across batch samples. Theorem G.1 derives an exact algebraic factorization into matrix multiplications and Hadamard products that strictly bounds memory to $O(n^2)$, making conditional distance correlation scalable and practical for mini-batch backpropagation.

Broad applicability to data modalities and variable types: Unlike group-based methods (e.g., GDRO, IRM) that necessitate categorical variables and discrete group partitions, DISCO natively accommodates continuous, categorical, and multivariate targets and biases within a unified metric framework.

Comprehensive empirical validation: Evaluated across six distinct datasets (vision and NLP, synthetic and real-world) against seven representative baselines, where DISCO variants consistently achieve competitive or superior results with fewer tunable hyperparameters.

Insightful counterfactual sensitivity and runtime analysis: The pathway-specific counterfactual analysis (Section 4.4, Appendix H.4) explicitly illustrates whether performance drops stem from lingering bias or target signal suppression, complemented by thorough wall-clock and GPU memory benchmarks in Appendix H.5.
weaknesses: Novelty of the conditional independence criterion itself: Enforcing $\hat{Y} \perp B \mid Y$ has been explored in prior fairness and invariant representation literature (e.g., separation criterion, Makar & D'Amour, Veitch et al., Quinzan et al.). While the SAM path-specific derivation is clarifying and unified, the criterion itself is well-established; the paper's primary algorithmic novelty lies in the distance correlation factorization.

Reliance on fully observed bias annotations: The causal stability guarantees strictly require that all bias attributes $B$ are observed during training. As noted in Section 2.2, when unobserved confounding $Z'$ is present without valid proxies, residual bias remains unblocked.

Kernel bandwidth sensitivity: The method requires tuning the kernel bandwidth parameter $\sigma_Y$ over the conditioning variable. Although the search grid in Table 5 is smaller than CIRCE's or HSCIC's, performance in kernel-based conditional dependence estimation remains sensitive to bandwidth choice, especially when $Y$ is continuous or high-dimensional.

strengths: Principled unification via SAM: The paper provides a clear structural causal framework (the Standard Anti-Causal Model) that systematically formalizes confounder, collider, and mediator biases, rigorously justifying why enforcing conditional independence $\hat{Y} \perp B \mid Y$ suffices to eliminate counterfactual indirect and spurious effects in anti-causal prediction.

Clever and impactful algorithmic contribution (sDISCO): Naive estimation of conditional distance correlation incurs an $O(n^3)$ memory bottleneck over batch size $n$. The proposed exact algebraic factorization via diagonal extraction identities and Hadamard operations reduces memory to $O(n^2)$ without compromising the exact sample V-statistic, making conditional distance correlation practical for gradient-based deep learning.

Broad applicability across variable modalities: Unlike many prior methods (e.g., GDRO, IRM, Fishr, c-MMD) that strictly require categorical targets or bias attributes, DISCO seamlessly accommodates combinations of continuous and discrete targets and biases, as demonstrated on both regression and classification tasks.

Comprehensive empirical validation: Evaluated across six diverse datasets (synthetic, facial image, vision benchmarks, and NLP) and compared against seven baselines. The empirical results demonstrate strong, consistent performance with fewer hyperparameters to tune compared to kernel baselines like CIRCE and HSCIC.

Thorough counterfactual sensitivity and computational profiling: The paper goes beyond standard test set accuracy by conducting path-specific counterfactual sensitivity experiments ($S_X, S_Y, \text{Acc}_{\text{ctf}}$) and detailed runtime/memory profiling across batch sizes, confirming sDISCO's scalability without out-of-memory errors.
weaknesses: Prior literature on the conditional independence criterion: The concept that enforcing conditional independence of predictions from bias given target ($\hat{Y} \perp B \mid Y$, closely linked to the fairness notion of separation) removes spurious correlation has been examined in related works (e.g., Veitch et al., 2021; Makar & D'Amour, 2023; Pogodin et al., 2022). While SAM formalizes this elegantly via path-specific counterfactuals, the observational condition itself is not entirely new.

Reliance on fully observed bias labels: The methodology operates strictly in the informed bias mitigation regime, requiring explicit annotations for all bias attributes during training. While acknowledging this limitation, the performance when bias annotations are noisy, incomplete, or partially unobserved warrants deeper exploration.

Sensitivity to conditioning kernel bandwidth: Estimating conditioning on continuous targets $Y$ relies on kernel density weighting (e.g., RBF bandwidth $h$). Performance in extreme conditioning settings or high-dimensional target vectors could be sensitive to this choice.

Minor presentation oversight: In Appendix A, a sentence contains an incomplete placeholder: 'Following the constructive feedback from regarding the presentation of our theoretical claims...', which should be cleaned up.

strengths: Principled Causal Formulation: The Standard Anti-Causal Model (SAM) provides an elegant, unified graphical and counterfactual framework that decomposes prediction total variation into counterfactually stable, indirect, and spurious components, giving clear causal grounding to the conditional independence criterion $\hat{Y} \perp B \mid Y$.

Novel and Efficient Estimator (sDISCO): The algebraic factorization in Theorem G.1 is clever and impactful. By utilizing the diagonal extraction identity for quadratic forms and Hadamard products, the authors reduce the memory requirement of computing the exact V-statistic from prohibitive $O(n^3)$ to $O(n^2)$, making conditional distance correlation fully practical and scalable for gradient-based deep learning.

Broad Versatility: Unlike several existing bias mitigation techniques that are strictly confined to categorical groups or environments (such as GDRO, IRM, and Fishr), DISCO naturally supports arbitrary combinations of continuous and categorical targets and biases.

Thorough Empirical Validation: The method is evaluated across six diverse datasets (synthetic, computer vision, and NLP), benchmarking against seven relevant baselines. In addition to standard bias-balanced accuracy, the paper evaluates counterfactual sensitivities ($S_X, S_Y$) and counterfactual accuracy/R2, demonstrating that the method specifically strips out spurious paths without destroying target predictive signal.

Comprehensive Computational Analysis: Appendix H.5 provides runtime and memory benchmarking demonstrating that sDISCO avoids out-of-memory errors on large batch sizes where naive formulations and DISCOm fail.
weaknesses: Incremental Novelty of the Independence Criterion: While the structural path-specific analysis via SAM is well-formulated, the criterion $\hat{Y} \perp B \mid Y$ itself (separation / conditional independence) is already well-established in algorithmic fairness and shortcut mitigation literature (e.g., Veitch et al., 2021; Makar & D'Amour, 2023; Quinzan et al., 2022). The conceptual advance is primarily in framing and unification rather than proposing a fundamentally new objective.

Performance Discrepancy Between DISCOm and sDISCO: In Table 2, the subsampled DISCOm noticeably outperforms the exact sDISCO on datasets such as YaleB (0.804 vs 0.770) and FairFace (0.860 vs 0.850). The manuscript does not adequately discuss why stochastic subsampling of reference points yields better test performance than evaluating the exact full-batch V-statistic (e.g., whether this acts as an implicit regularizer).

Curse of Dimensionality in Conditioning: Estimating conditional dependence relies on kernel smoothing via $W$ over the conditioning variable $Y$. While effective for scalar targets, kernel density estimation scales poorly as the dimension of conditioning variables increases; the paper does not empirically evaluate or deeply discuss settings with high-dimensional conditioning sets.

Minor Editorial Artifact: In Appendix A, there is a visible artifact from revision: 'Following the constructive feedback from regarding the presentation of our theoretical claims...', where a word or reviewer reference appears to have been omitted or inadvertently deleted during drafting.

strengths: Principled causal formulation: The Standard Anti-Causal Model (SAM) provides an intuitive and unified causal framework that treats confounders, colliders, and mediators systematically under an anti-causal prediction setting, neatly decomposing total variation into direct, indirect, and spurious effects.

Novel and efficient estimator: The proposed DISCO_m and particularly sDISCO offer a practical, differentiable, and computationally efficient realization of conditional distance correlation suitable for mini-batch backpropagation in deep neural networks, supporting continuous, categorical, and multivariate variables without requiring adversarial minimax optimization.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The method is validated across five diverse benchmark datasets (dSprites, synthetic Blobs, YaleB, FairFace, Waterbirds) against strong baselines (GDRO, CIRCE, HSCIC, c-MMD, Adversarial), achieving competitive or state-of-the-art results.

Insightful counterfactual diagnostic: The pathway-specific counterfactual sensitivity and accuracy analysis (Section 4.4 and Appendix E.4) effectively explains why certain baselines fail (e.g., suppressing spurious features at the expense of task-relevant signals) and validates model behavior under unobserved/partial bias settings.
weaknesses: Incremental conceptual novelty regarding the core criterion: The conditional independence criterion Y_hat _|_ B | Y is well-established in the algorithmic fairness literature (where it corresponds to separation / equalized odds) and in counterfactually invariant prediction (e.g., Veitch et al., 2021; Pogodin et al., 2022; Makar et al., 2022). While the causal pathway synthesis under SAM is neat, the target optimization objective is not fundamentally new.

Informal theoretical guarantees: The proofs of consistency for DISCO_m and sDISCO in Appendices D.3 and D.4 are primarily high-level proof sketches rather than rigorous, full mathematical proofs (e.g., lacking finite-sample concentration bounds, formal rate analysis, or handling of SGD mini-batch sampling bias).

Lack of analysis on batch size sensitivity and computational overhead: Distance correlation estimators require computing pairwise distance matrices of size n x n per batch. The manuscript would benefit from an explicit empirical ablation on mini-batch size sensitivity as well as wall-clock training time / memory profiling against baselines like CIRCE and GDRO.

strengths: Principled causal motivation: The Standard Anti-Causal Model (SAM) provides a clear and unifying structural framework that formalizes how confounder, collider, and mediator biases can be treated uniformly via the conditional independence criterion $\hat{Y} \perp B \mid Y$.

Versatile dependence estimator: By adapting conditional distance correlation to differentiable mini-batch learning, the proposed estimators (DISCOm and sDISCO) handle arbitrary combinations of variable types (continuous, categorical, multidimensional) without requiring complex adversarial architectures or kernel inversions.

Solid empirical performance across domains: Evaluated on five diverse datasets across both regression and classification settings, the methods show strong and consistent performance compared to representative baselines (GDRO, c-MMD, CIRCE, HSCIC, and Adversarial training).

Insightful counterfactual diagnostic analysis: The pathway-specific counterfactual analysis in Section 4.4 and Appendix E.4 offers useful insights into how methods balance bias reduction against preserving direct task signal.
weaknesses: Informal theoretical analysis for consistency: The proofs for Propositions 2 and 3 (in Appendices D.3 and D.4) are high-level proof sketches rather than rigorous proofs. In particular, the consistency of sDISCO's globally weighted centering with kernel regression requires careful asymptotic analysis of kernel bandwidth, boundary bias, and U-statistic degenerate components, which is currently hand-waved.

Lack of runtime and computational complexity evaluation: A primary stated contribution of sDISCO is resolving the computational intractability of conditional distance correlation for deep learning. However, the paper lacks empirical wall-clock timing comparisons, GPU memory footprints, or formal asymptotic complexity comparisons against DISCOm, CIRCE, and HSCIC across varying batch sizes and feature dimensions.

Omission of the discrete conditioning simplification: In three out of the five benchmark datasets (YaleB, FairFace, Waterbirds), the conditioning target $Y$ is discrete/categorical. When conditioning on a discrete variable, conditional independence $\hat{Y} \perp B \mid Y$ decomposes into standard marginal independences $\hat{Y} \perp B$ evaluated within each slice $Y=y$. The paper does not discuss this simplification or evaluate whether sDISCO provides benefits over evaluating standard distance correlation stratified by class.

strengths: Unifying Causal Framework: The paper provides a clear causal formalization (SAM) that frames confounders, colliders, and mediators uniformly under anti-causal prediction, neatly connecting graphical causal analysis with counterfactual pathway decompositions.

Novel Differentiable Estimators: Adapting conditional distance correlation into differentiable, mini-batch compatible estimators (DISCOm and sDISCO) overcomes a long-standing computational hurdle of kernel/distance-based conditional dependence measures in deep learning.

Broad Applicability: Unlike many baseline approaches (e.g., GDRO, c-MMD) that are restricted to categorical attributes, DISCO naturally handles arbitrary combinations of continuous and discrete target and bias variables without requiring adversarial min-max optimization.

Comprehensive Empirical and Pathway Evaluation: Experiments span five diverse datasets, supplemented by fine-grained counterfactual pathway analysis that verifies the actual suppression of spurious sensitivities.
weaknesses: Limited Originality of the Core Causal Criterion: The condition $\hat{Y} \perp B \mid Y$ for counterfactual invariance and bias mitigation in anti-causal settings is already well established in prior literature (e.g., Veitch et al., 2021; Makar et al., 2022; Pogodin et al., 2022; Quinzan et al., 2022). The paper's conceptual framing via SAM is largely an incremental re-derivation of known invariance principles.

Significant Performance Gap Between DISCOm and sDISCO: While sDISCO is motivated theoretically as an efficient, consistent single-shot counterpart to DISCOm, it suffers noticeable performance drops in several benchmarks (e.g., dSprites drops from 0.688 to 0.619; YaleB drops from 0.804 to 0.694). The paper provides insufficient analysis of why sDISCO degrades in finite mini-batch regimes.

Lack of Mini-Batch Sensitivity Analysis: Kernel regression-based conditioning in small mini-batches (e.g., 64–128) is susceptible to high variance and finite-sample bias, especially when conditioning on continuous or multi-dimensional variables. The manuscript lacks an empirical ablation investigating sensitivity to batch size.

Absence of Wall-Clock Efficiency Benchmarks: Although computational scalability and efficiency over previous formulations and baselines are central claims, the manuscript does not provide empirical run-time or memory benchmarks comparing DISCOm, sDISCO, CIRCE, HSCIC, and Adversarial training.

Model Selection on Unbiased Validation Sets: The tuning and model selection rely entirely on an unbiased/balanced validation set. In realistic out-of-distribution scenarios, unbiased validation sets are rarely accessible, and performance can be sensitive to this assumption.
